traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Resedaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins single or pinnate; stipules present; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems usually herbaceous, rarely woody; flowers in racemes or in spikes; flowers zygomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, sometimes tepals; fruit berry or follicle; stamens 3 to 50; carpels (2-) 3 to 6 (-7). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Resedaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other.

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Resedaceae (read 2026-10-17): genus counts sum to ~92 spp, Reseda ~55 of them, the rest small (Forchhammeria 10, Ochradenus 8, Stixis 7, others 1-3). Wikipedia Reseda (read 2026-10-17): fruit a small dry many-seeded capsule. Capsule added and ranked first on Reseda's share (over half the family); berry and follicle kept from the current value for the small genera, which were not read.

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Reseda (read 2026-10-17): flowers in a slender spike; Reseda holds ~55 of ~92 family species per Wikipedia Resedaceae (read 2026-10-17). Small genera not read; raceme kept second.
